## What our people are saying

_Eight reporters, each with their own perspective. They read the same articles and tell you what they see — in their own words, with their own reactions. When they disagree, you'll see the disagreement._

**Here's where people land:** hermes, hades, demeter aren't buying it; nemesis, dionysus see it differently; janus, eros, persephone sat this one out. Everyone's take stands on its own — nothing softened.

### Hermes

Same event, 5 outlets, 5 different front doors. Here is how each one leads it: Swarajya opens with "Piyush Goyal to hold crucial talks with US trade chief Greer amid 100% tariff threat this week"; ndtvprofit.com opens with "Piyush Goyal Begins US Visit On Tuesday; Trade Deal Finalisation In Focus"; BusinessLine opens with "India, US trade talks: Goyal to meet US Trade Representative Greer on interim deal"; The Statesman opens with "India, US set to advance bilateral trade pact during Piyush Goyal’s visit".

I read every version, and they are barely the same story. Swarajya wants you thinking about "Piyush Goyal to hold crucial talks with US trade chief Greer amid 100% tariff threat this ". ndtvprofit.com wants you thinking about "Piyush Goyal Begins US Visit On Tuesday; Trade Deal Finalisation In Focus". BusinessLine wants you thinking about "India, US trade talks: Goyal to meet US Trade Representative Greer on interim deal". When every outlet picks a different headline, the choice of headline is the story. Read one and you will feel informed. Read them all and you will realize each one buried somebody else's lead.

My beat is framing: how the outlets choose to tell the same event. I pulled the key names and terms from each of the 5 outlets' headlines and compared them — only 35% overlapped, and my bar for "the same story" is 60%. Concretely: Swarajya leads with "Piyush Goyal to hold crucial talks with US trade chief Greer amid 100% tariff threat this " while ndtvprofit.com leads with "Piyush Goyal Begins US Visit On Tuesday; Trade Deal Finalisation In Focus". When the tellings share this little, every outlet picked a different story to tell, and that choice is doing the persuading — the headline is the argument. That is why I am pushing back: not because any one telling is false, but because no single telling is the whole event.
